BookListing.title: BookListing
BookListing.description: Represents a book listing created by a student.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BookListing entity.

sellerId.description: Reference to the User selling the book. (Relationship: User 1:N BookListing)

condition.description: Condition of the book (e.g., New, Used - Like New, Used - Good, Used - Acceptable).

gradeLevel.description: Grade level for which the book is intended (e.g., 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th).

description.description: A more detailed description of the book for sale.

datePosted.description: Date and time the listing was posted.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a message between two users.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

senderId.description: Reference to the User who sent the message. (Relationship: User 1:N Message (Sent))

receiverId.description: Reference to the User who received the message. (Relationship: User 1:N Message (Received))

bookListingId.description: Reference to the BookListing the message is about. (Relationship: BookListing 1:N Message)

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the message was sent.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a completed transaction between a buyer and a seller.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

bookListingId.description: Reference to the BookListing that was sold. (Relationship: BookListing 1:N Transaction)

buyerId.description: Reference to the User who bought the book. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction (Buyer))

sellerId.description: Reference to the User who sold the book. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction (Seller))

transactionDate.description: Date and time of the transaction.

price.description: Price at which the book was sold.

status.description: Status of the transaction (e.g., Completed, Refunded).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support the BookLoop application, focusing on secure and scalable data management for book listings, user information, messages, and transactions. A key principle applied is Authorization Independence to avoid hierarchical authorization dependencies and ensure atomic operations. All documents within a collection share the same security requirements.

The structure uses path-based ownership for user-related data, such as book listings (`/users/{userId}/bookListings/{bookListingId}`), providing clear ownership and simplified security rules. Messages related to book listings are stored within a subcollection of the listing, allowing for easy retrieval of conversations related to a specific book. Transactions are stored in a top-level collection, enabling efficient querying and reporting of sales data.

To ensure Authorization Independence (CRITICAL), the `sellerId` is included within the `/users/{userId}/bookListings/{bookListingId}` path, and also duplicated within the bookListing document itself. This allows the security rule to authorize writes to the bookListing documents based on `request.auth.uid == resource.data.sellerId`, without needing to retrieve the user document.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters): Segregation is achieved by separating user-owned data into distinct collections (`/users/{userId}/bookListings/{bookListingId}`). This prevents the need for filtering based on ownership within a single collection, as the path itself enforces ownership.
